sentences.text: No retrieved publication mentions Vescimonas sanitatis by name, so the statements below concern the genus Vescimonas.
Vescimonas was proposed for Gram-stain-negative, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, non-motile rods isolated from human faeces and placed in the family Ruminococcaceae.
A study of human obesity reported that the diversity of the genus Vescimonas, and its abundance, were negatively correlated with body mass index.
A study of populations in Malaysia reported Vescimonas among genera more prevalent in urban individuals, while Prevotella and Cryptobacteroides were enriched in rural populations.
